page.layout: One page of text. Top: a continuation of the dedication in larger type, with the dateline beneath it. Middle: a Latin elegiac poem of four couplets, indented, followed by a Greek poem of two couplets. Below: the dedicatory signature, centred or right-aligned. Bottom: a woodcut ornament (not text). No margin notes, no running head, no catchword.

main_text.p: bene de me mereri, quod & facis, perge. E museo, Nonis Martij, Anni Christiani MDXC.

p.i: Accipe, Mecœnas, nostra quod mittere donum Musa, quod pridem mittere debuerant.
Accipe: deinde boni placidus quoque consule quaso, Dobbine, Aonij summe patrone chori.
Qua do, ne videas quali sint condita plectro, Sed qua sint potius condita mente, vide.
Salue Mecœnas, Aula pia gloria, salue, Meq; patrocinio perge fouere tuo.

page.notes: The Greek verse (two couplets) could not be read letter by letter at this scan resolution; marked illegible with approximate letter counts. The Greek is printed in Greek letters and must be checked against the original. "Meq;" in the last Latin line is uncertain; the abbreviation may be a form of "Mecœnas" or "Mecaenas". "Qua do" in the third line appears as printed. The dateline "clo. lo. xc" is rendered per the reversed-C rule as MDXC. The woodcut ornament below the signature is decoration and is not transcribed. Faint show-through of text from the reverse side appears at the right edge and is excluded.
